name: Aftab Pureval
title: Mayor
bio:
Aftab Pureval is the 70th Mayor of Cincinnati. He was raised in Southwest, Ohio, the son of first-generation Americans. He is making history as Cincinnati’s first Asian- American Mayor. He has made equitable economic growth a top priority of his administration, as well as a comprehensive reform and improvement of public safety, affordable housing, and environmental action.

Since taking office, Mayor Aftab has guided Cincinnati through a significant economic recovery, while advancing the City’s key strategic priorities for equitable growth.

Early accomplishments include establishing the City’s first-ever annual commitment to an affordable housing trust fund, leading on a comprehensive zoning reform to bring more housing options to neighborhoods, and implementing a new policy to send unarmed mental health professionals to some nonviolent 911 calls. Under his leadership, the City’s budget was balanced after multiple years of structural deficits, and the City committed for the first time to carbon neutrality by 2050.

name: Abby Grimm
title: Director of Engagement & Experience
bio:
Abby Grimm is a civic-minded connector, community builder, and one of the driving forces behind StartupCincy Week. At Cintrifuse, she stewards the StartupCincy community - convening entrepreneurs, investors, support organizations, and community partners to move Cincinnati’s innovation ecosystem forward and ultimately advance the region as a whole.

Her passion for building a more connected, vibrant Cincinnati extends to her role as Vice Chair of the OTR Chamber of Commerce, and Founder of RADICO, a civic impact studio taking bold concepts from idea to action. Across her work, she’s happiest at the intersection of big dreams, interesting people, and making Cincinnati the best place to build and to thrive.

name: Valerie Jacobs
title: Founder & CEO
bio:
Valerie Jacobs helps organizations see what's coming next, before everyone else does. As a trend forecaster and futurist, she has spent her career decoding shifts in culture, consumer behavior, and business, then turning that foresight into real growth. Over her career at LPK, she held several roles in the C-suite, using her forecasting instincts to help shape the direction of the company and its clients.

Today, through her own consultancy, Valerie Jacobs Futures, she works with organizations like The Coca-Cola Company, Nationwide, Fifth Third Bank, and The Milken Institute to help leaders build the kind of foresight that makes bold decisions feel a lot less risky. She holds a Master of Design from the University of Cincinnati, teaches trend forecasting there as an Adjunct Instructor, and serves as a Senior Fellow of the Design Futures Council. She has a long history with Cintrifuse, and her work has been featured in Forbes, Inc., and Vogue.

name: Kara Willis
title: Program Manager
bio: Kara Willis is a marketing, events, and community engagement professional with a career focused on bringing people, ideas, and experiences together. She currently serves as Program Manager for RedHawk50 at Miami University’s John W. Altman Institute for Entrepreneurship, where she works with alumni entrepreneurs and the broader Miami University entrepreneurship community. Kara also serves as Marketing Director at The Mercantile Library in Cincinnati, leading marketing, membership engagement, programming, and communications for one of the country’s oldest member-supported libraries. Throughout her career, she has worked across marketing, events, entrepreneurship, community building, and brand strategy, with a particular passion for creating memorable experiences and developing programs that help people connect. Her work is driven by a belief that great marketing is about more than promotion. It is about building communities, telling meaningful stories, and creating opportunities for people to engage with organizations in authentic and unexpected ways.

name: The Mz.Icar Collective
bio: Mz.Icar Collective is an interdisciplinary group of artists creating bold, community-centered public art that blends storytelling, material culture, and speculative imagination. Their collaborative practice spans murals, sculptural installations, textiles, projection mapping, and immersive environments that invite audiences into experiences of joy, reflection, and belonging. Rooted in deep engagement with local communities and cultural histories, their work amplifies underrepresented voices while exploring how emerging technologies like augmented reality and interactive projection can support cultural storytelling and memory-making. Their projects have been installed across cities including Boston, Brooklyn, Cincinnati, Green Bay, and Philadelphia, and have been featured in collaborations with festivals and institutions such as BLINK and The Roots Picnic.

name: Cedric Michael Cox & Studio 181 Brent Keltch
bio:
Cedric Michael Cox creates vibrant paintings that fuse abstraction and recognizable imagery into rhythmic compositions inspired by music, nature, architecture, and art history, ranging from cubist geometric forms to surreal cityscapes and floral-like environments. Brent’s bio: Brent Keltch is a multifaceted Cincinnati-based visual artist, sculptor, and gallery owner. Operating out of Studio 181 at the historic Essex Studios colony in Walnut Hills, his work blends diverse artistic disciplines with community advocacy.
